title: Pewaukee confirmed below breakeven for a second straight period: True ROAS 0.90 again on $555 spend, with tracked orders cut in half (35.4 -> 17.7)
detail: Last week Pewaukee was flagged as a possible one-period drop. It is not — True ROAS landed at 0.90 for the second consecutive window on a different date range, so this is now a confirmed problem rather than noise. Tracked order revenue fell $874 -> $499 (-43%) while spend came down only $805 -> $555 (-31%), and order count halved from 35.4 to 17.7. It is the only store in the account below 1.0 and the 3rd-largest spender. Every other store is at 1.07 or above. Blended ROAS (3.71 vs 3.58) actually looks like an improvement and hides the problem completely. Action: cut Pewaukee's budget ~$150-200/period now rather than waiting another cycle, and place an actual test order through the Pewaukee online-ordering flow — an order count dropping by half while impressions hold is more consistent with a broken or hard-to-find ordering path than with soft demand. Standing caveat: in-store visits driven by these local ads are not captured here, so 0.90 is the measurable floor, not the full return.

title: Budget still top-heavy: Brookfield and Milwaukee take $694 each (27% of Google spend) at True ROAS 1.25 and 1.16, while the 1.7+ tier — Middleton, Sun Prairie, Whitefish Bay — is capped below them
detail: Both big spenders improved this period (Brookfield 0.84 -> 1.25, Milwaukee flat at 1.16), so this is less severe than last week, but the ranking is still inverted. Brookfield and Milwaukee are the #1 and #2 spenders at $694 apiece yet rank 7th and 9th of 11 on True ROAS. Meanwhile Middleton returned 1.78 on just $445 ($791 of tracked orders), Sun Prairie 1.72 on $551 ($948), and Whitefish Bay 1.71 on $552 ($942) — the three best stores in the account, all funded at or below the two weakest large spenders. Middleton is the clearest case: it produces more tracked order revenue than Milwaukee on 36% less spend. Action: raise Middleton's budget cap first (largest proven gap), then Sun Prairie and Whitefish Bay, funded by a ~$200 trim to Milwaukee. Total spend unchanged, more tracked order revenue. Milwaukee has now been flagged four periods running — if dine-in volume is the reason to keep funding it at $694, confirm that against Toast same-store sales and close the item either way.

title: Monona slipped 1.72 -> 1.45 on a 42% revenue drop, and its average tracked order value fell from $34 to $24
detail: Monona's tracked order revenue fell $1,042 -> $601 (-42%) while spend came down only 31% ($605 -> $416), taking True ROAS from 1.72 to 1.45. It is still comfortably profitable on tracked orders and remains a top-half store, so this is not urgent. What makes it worth watching is the composition: order count fell only 19% (30.6 -> 24.9) while revenue fell 42%, meaning average tracked order value dropped from roughly $34 to $24. That is a bigger swing than order volume alone explains and points to a product-mix or promotion shift rather than a demand loss. Action: no budget change this cycle. Cross-check Monona's ticket average against the product-mix dashboard — if the store is genuinely selling smaller tickets, that is an operations question, not a media one.

title: Meta rose a third straight period to $1,145 (+$403) and is now 18% of all paid spend with still zero purchase tracking
detail: Meta has climbed from ~$660 to $741 to $1,145 across three reads while remaining entirely traffic-objective. It buys efficient traffic — 3,791 landing-page views at $0.30/LPV, improved from $0.32 — but none of the seven campaigns fire a purchase event, so nearly one paid dollar in five now sits outside the True-ROAS framework that governs every Google decision above. The growth is concentrated in 'brookfield sales 0726' ($336, up from $93) and the two new campus campaigns, UIUC ($82) and UW ($50). This gap has widened every period it has been raised. Action: installing the Meta Pixel purchase event on the Toast order-confirmation page is now the single highest-leverage measurement fix in the account — it would bring $1,145/period under the same standard as Google. Also still outstanding: migrate off the legacy personal-named ad account (act_35967094).

title: Account True ROAS held at 1.39 (from 1.20) and two prior recommendations closed out: Champaign reached 1.32 and Top Locations wound down to $49
detail: Spend fell 31% ($7,317 -> $5,075) while tracked order revenue fell only 19% ($8,747 -> $7,071), holding True ROAS at 1.39 — essentially flat against last week's 1.42 and well above the 1.05 low. The tracking-break theory raised two weeks ago is now definitively closed: three consecutive windows have read 1.39-1.42 with 9 of 11 stores improving. Two closed items: (1) Champaign, flagged as chronically unprofitable at 0.30-0.47, has climbed to 1.32 — $374 of tracked orders on $283 spend, revenue up 208% on a smaller budget. The trim worked and the funnel is fine; hold it at ~$285 and stop treating it as a problem store. (2) The Top Locations pause fully took effect — spend collapsed $595 -> $49. One caveat on this period's read: daily conversion value tapers over the final four days (8/25-8/28), which is normal GA4 attribution lag on recent dates, so the true figure for this window will likely revise slightly upward.

title: Meta's 'Catering Traffic 0326 video' is still the worst cost/LPV at $0.45 while the new campus campaigns are the cheapest in the account at $0.22-0.23
detail: Catering improved from $0.58 to $0.45 per landing-page view but remains 50% above the $0.30 account average and worst of the seven campaigns for a third period — $224 spend for 494 LPVs. At the other end, the two campaigns launched this period are the most efficient traffic in the account: UW Campus at $0.217/LPV and UIUC Campus at $0.229/LPV, both well clear of the $0.26-0.30 cluster. Campus targeting is working and is worth more budget on traffic efficiency alone. Catering is a genuinely different objective and its higher cost may be justified — but nothing in the account measures catering inquiries, so there is no way to tell. Action: shift a portion of Catering's $224 into the two campus campaigns while they are proving out, or define a catering-inquiry conversion event so that spend can be judged on something other than LPV cost.
